result:
Fixed. Root cause and fix, in `src/jinja2/idtracking.py`'s `Symbols.branch_update()`:

- When the id-tracking visitor processes an `if`/`elif`/`else`, it merges the three branch scopes (`body`, `elif`, `else`) back into the parent scope. The buggy version counted, per name, how many of the 3 branches stored it, and if a name was stored in **all 3** it skipped re-resolving that name's load â€” on the (incorrect) assumption that exhaustive assignment meant the load path could never matter, i.e. it treated the name as pure store with no possible reference to its prior value.
- That assumption breaks the general case: skipping resolution left the name's load instruction whatever was last merged in rather than properly re-deriving it (alias/resolve/undefined), which under the right combination of nested scopes surfaces as the variable evaluating to `undefined`.
- The fix (matching the change now shipped in current Jinja2) removes the branch-count optimization entirely: it computes the set of names stored across all branches, subtracts names already stored before the `if`, and always resolves everything that's left â€” regardless of whether it was set in 1, 2, or all 3 branches.

I verified the change against the actual upstream jinja2 fix (diffed this repo's `idtracking.py` against the current PyPI release, which contains the identical fix), and ran the full test suite: 907 passed, no regressions.
